observables.name: l_g_fitted_tail
observables.prediction_source: paper Table 1, l_g = 10.7 um / d = 0.8 um
observables.derivation: Where phi -> 0 the fluid is ideal and the profile is exactly n0 exp(-z/l_g), so the apparent decay length IS l_g. Quantified on the CS-equilibrium profile: over [55, 100] d it has Z_CS(phi_eff) <= 1.019 and an apparent l_g of 13.495 d, +0.90 % against the imposed 13.375 -- inside the 5 % tolerance, so excluded volume cannot fake a failure here. ⚠ The DENSE window gives 15.44 d (+15.5 %) on the same profile, so a check against 13.375 there would call a correct result a bug; that fit is reported separately as a hypothesis.
observables.note: the decay length over the DILUTE TAIL, h in [55, 100] d. ★ This is the implementation check, not the dense-window fit

observables.name: l_g_fitted_dense
observables.derivation: HYPOTHESIS: the prediction 15.442 d comes from integrating the Carnahan-Starling hydrostatic ODE for this cell and fitting the same window, so a mismatch says the WCA fluid's profile differs from the CS one -- which is the same question P3 asks, read off the profile instead of the EOS. The ideal-gas value 13.375 is 13.4 % away, so the two are separable.
observables.note: the apparent decay length over the dense window h in [2, 80.2] d, where excluded volume flattens the profile

observables.name: Z_dilute_tail
observables.derivation: With n = n0 exp(-z/l_g), the integral of rho above z is exactly l_g rho(z), so Z = 1 identically. Any error in the cumulative sum, the bin width or the l_g used shows up here before it reaches the EOS.
observables.note: Z -> 1 as phi -> 0. Costs nothing and catches a wrong hydrostatic read

observables.name: Z_dev_wmean_vs_CS_eff
observables.derivation: HYPOTHESIS, not a check: the simulation imposes a WCA core and imposes no equation of state at all, so a mismatch is a result about how well a soft core stands in for a hard sphere. The 2 % band is INHERITED from this repository's own prior measurement of the same substitution (-0.32 % at phi ~ 0.10, -0.51 % at phi ~ 0.21 at eps = 1 kT), not invented. phi_eff = phi (d_BH/d)^3 with d_BH/d = 0.9048.
observables.note: Poisson-weighted mean of (Z - CS(phi_eff))/CS over the window, in percent. ★ THE answering quantity of intake/sediment-pmma-3d/goal.yaml

observables.name: Z_dev_wmean_vs_CS_nominal
observables.derivation: CS(phi_eff) and CS(phi_nominal) differ by -17.05 % at the wall of this cell, so the two are separable by this measurement. No prediction is attached: this number IS the discriminator.
observables.note: the same weighted mean WITHOUT the Barker-Henderson mapping. The GAP between this and the line above is what says whether the mapping is required

observables.name: Z_dev_max_vs_CS_eff
observables.note: the LARGEST single-slab deviation. Reported without a verdict on purpose: at 200 frames a slab carries ~2.7 % Poisson error, so the max over ~40 slabs is ~7 % from noise alone. It is here to show the noise floor beside the weighted mean, not to be compared with 2 %

observables.name: Z_at_densest_slab
observables.derivation: One slab, so it carries the full Poisson error (~1/sqrt(counts)); the 8 % tolerance is that error plus room, not a physics claim. Its value is that CS(phi_eff) and CS(phi_nominal) are furthest apart here, so it is where the mapping question is sharpest.
observables.note: the single most discriminating point: phi = 0.1043, phi_eff = 0.0773, 6858 counts. CS(phi_nominal) there is 1.5505, which is the alternative this point separates from

observables.name: profile_halves_chi2_nu
observables.prediction_source: Poisson counting error on each half-window profile
observables.derivation: chi^2/nu = mean over bins of (r1-r2)^2/(var1+var2) with r = counts/frame and var = counts/frames^2. The 100 % tolerance means the band is [0, 2]: a value of 2 is twice the Poisson variance, which is a real drift rather than a marginal one. Required by the sealed analysis plan's step 3, which the run output could NOT support before this was added.
observables.note: ★ THE STATIONARITY TEST, over 159 bins. The primary arm starts FROM the Carnahan-Starling profile, so it cannot demonstrate equilibrium by arriving anywhere -- only by NOT MOVING. chi^2/nu between the first and second halves of the production window is 1.0 for a stationary profile and larger if it drifted. The mean height shifted +1.757 % between halves, which says which way

observables.name: profile_half_shift_pct
observables.note: the mean height of the profile in the second half against the first, in percent. Signed on purpose: the convergence arm must move DOWNWARD (negative) and the primary arm must not move at all

observables.name: D_xy
observables.derivation: x and y are unconfined and periodic, so the lateral MSD is 4 D t with D = D_0 = 1 in these units. ⚠ the VERTICAL MSD saturates at ~l_g^2 and must not be fit (the card's gate table). Excluded volume at phi <~ 0.16 lowers the long-time D by a few percent, hence 10 % rather than 5 %.
observables.note: lateral self-diffusion in reduced units -- the clock, checked against itself

observables.name: phi_wall_measured_vs_cs_eff
observables.derivation: the highest-density bin below h = 1.5 d. Independent of the EOS estimator and of the hydrostatic integral, so it is a different KIND of evidence (A1) from Z_dev_wmean rather than a restatement
observables.note: ★ A THIRD DISCRIMINATOR, and the cheapest to read. The Monte Carlo puts CS(phi_eff) at 0.1118 +- 0.0019 and CS(phi_nominal) at 0.1029 +- 0.0018 -- 4.7 sigma apart at the primary arm and 7.5 at L_xy = 24. The ideal-gas start is 0.1589, far above both

observables.name: phi_wall_measured
observables.note: the highest local volume fraction the profile reached -- how far up the CS curve this run got

observables.name: Z_dev_wmean_block_sem
observables.derivation: std(ddof=1)/sqrt(n) over the per-block values of the same weighted mean. NaN when fewer than 3 blocks reduce -- a zero error bar is worse than none.
observables.note: ★ THE ERROR BAR THE CAMPAIGN'S POWER RESTS ON, from 16 of 16 blocks of this run's own production window. ⚠ The design-power Monte Carlo said 0.38 % by drawing every frame as an independent Poisson realisation; the measured integrated autocorrelation time of the mean height is 86-132 frames out of 478, so a 4 tau_sed window carries N_eff = 3.6-5.5 independent samples. Whatever this number is, it is the one with correlation in it

observables.name: l_g_dense_block_sem
observables.note: the second discriminator's own error bar, same method. The two hypotheses are 1.069 d apart, so this is what says whether that gap is resolvable

observables.name: phi_wall_block_sem
observables.note: the third discriminator's own error bar. The two hypotheses are 0.0089 apart

observables.name: Z_dilute_tail_block_sem
observables.note: ⚠ the GRAVITY GATE's own error bar, and the number that says whether its sealed 10 % band was ever a gate. The Monte Carlo said 2.9 %

observables.name: min_sep_placed
observables.note: closest pair at t=0. Below ~0.8 d the WCA core starts to set dt
